sentiment_score_definition: x <= -0.35: Bearish; -0.35 < x <= -0.15: Somewhat-Bearish; -0.15 < x < 0.15: Neutral; 0.15 <= x < 0.35: Somewhat_Bullish; x >= 0.35: Bullish
relevance_score_definition: 0 < x <= 1, with a higher score indicating higher relevance.

feed.title: Colgate India names Manish Anandani as new CEO

feed.title: Tesla Controls 59% of the U.S. EV Market -- Its Highest Share Since 2023
feed.summary: Tesla's U.S. EV market share has increased to 59%, a level not seen since 2023, despite a 25% stock drop this year. While the company's revenue grew, profitability decreased due to significant investments in AI, Optimus, and robotaxis, leading to negative free cash flow. This creates volatility for investors, balancing a strong core business against speculative ancillary projects.

feed.title: Berkshire Hathaway Trims Bank of America Stake by $1.7 Billion, Adds to Delta Air Lines

feed.title: Corteva’s Field Trials Didn’t Undermine Its Seed-Patent Rights
feed.summary: A federal judge ruled against Inari Agriculture Inc., affirming the validity of Corteva AgriScience LLC's seed patents. This decision comes ahead of a trial in Delaware where Inari faces infringement accusations from Corteva.

feed.title: Delta Air Lines Planning To Leverage AI To Increase Profits By 50%, CEO Says
feed.summary: Delta Air Lines is planning to implement AI across various operations to boost profits by 50%, aiming to increase its operating margin from 10% to 15%. CEO Ed Bastian emphasized that AI, which he calls "augmented intelligence," will help the airline make better-informed decisions, cut costs by reallocating staff, and improve efficiency in areas like airfare pricing, crew recovery, and maintenance. The airline stressed that this initiative will not lead to immediate job losses and clarified that its AI-powered pricing will not target individuals with discriminatory fares, but rather enhance market competitiveness.

feed.title: Boeing engineers, technical workers reject contract offer
feed.summary: Boeing engineers and technical workers have rejected a four-year contract offer from the company, union officials announced. The Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace (SPEEA), representing 17,000 members, also voted to authorize a strike if a new agreement isn't reached by October. Key sticking points include the proposed wage increases, which are capped at 3% and tied to inflation and individual performance, a figure several members believe will not keep pace with the rising Consumer Price Index in their primary work area.

feed.title: Just 16 Days: Delta Air Lines Schedules 4 Routes To & From Orlando For Peak Holiday Travel

feed.title: Eastern Oregon food processor points fingers in nitrate pollution lawsuit
feed.summary: Lamb Weston, an Eastern Oregon food processor, is being sued by residents for alleged nitrate pollution in the Lower Umatilla Basin. In response, Lamb Weston has accused J.R. Simplot Co. and Shearer’s Foods of also contributing to the pollution and has asked the court to include them in the lawsuit, arguing for an equitable share of liability if found at fault. The residents fear this move could complicate and delay their case, which is currently scheduled for a jury trial in June 2027.
